title: Two Pills Under the Lamp
youtube_title: She brought the sweet half pill back. The doctor went pale.
logline: Nora takes the half pill to Dr. Brandt, who sets a real one beside it and sees at once that it's wrong. Grant has already beaten her to the hospital.
hook: Exam room, desk lamp, two pills side by side: one bitten, one whole. Dr. Brandt looks for a long time. "What I prescribed isn't sweet. And that's not the imprint."
mid_hook: Dr. Brandt: "Who gave you the pills every day?" Nora: "My husband. Every morning. On the table." The doctor's pen stops above the chart.
extra_hooks: Back row of the waiting area, Peg sits bolt upright with her ledger on her knees, eyes fixed on the sign down the hall: OUTPATIENT PHARMACY.
conflict: Nora needs proof the pill isn't what her doctor prescribed. Dr. Brandt can see the difference, but looking isn't proof: the half pill goes to the lab, three days.
turn: Nora expects to hear she's overthinking it. Instead Dr. Brandt seals the half pill in an evidence bag and dates it in her own hand. Nora isn't unstable. Someone switched her pills.

cliffhanger.text: Nora steps off the elevator. Behind a lobby pillar, Grant hands flowers and a gift box to the doctor's assistant: "My wife's not herself. Whatever she says, don't take it seriously." He turns and walks toward her pillar.
cliffhanger.question: Will he spot her in the lobby?

spectacle: Hard white lamplight on a black desk mat: two near-identical white pills side by side, one stroke of the imprint deep, the other shallow.
glamour_shot: Nora sits in the window light of the exam room, hands folded on her knees, chin slightly raised as she listens, eyes very still.
general_payoffs: Dr. Brandt confirms the half pill isn't what she prescribed

title: Nothing But Sugar
youtube_title: Her husband called her unstable. Then the lab results came.
logline: Nora slips past Grant in the lobby and waits three days for the lab. The result: no active ingredient. And the pharmacy still knows who picked up her pills every month.
hook: Grant is two steps from the pillar when Peg stands up from the waiting chairs and blocks him. "Grant. What are you doing here?" He stops. "Mom?" Peg: "Eye appointment."
mid_hook: Three days later, Dr. Brandt slides the lab report across. "No active ingredient detected. It's sugar." Then: "He came for your records two days ago. I didn't give them."
conflict: Nora needs a piece of paper that speaks. The lab proves the pill was fake. It can't prove who switched it.
turn: Nora thinks the lab report is the answer. Dr. Brandt says one more place remembers: the pharmacy logs who signs for every pickup, and Nora can request her own record.

cliffhanger.text: At the outpatient pharmacy window, the printer spits out a page. Dale Hutchins runs a finger down the rows. "Picked up every month. Signed by—" He turns the page around and slides it to her.
cliffhanger.question: Who picked up her pills?

spectacle: A lab report of empty columns, row after row, and one word printed in the last box: sugar.
glamour_shot: Under the cold light of the pharmacy window, waist-length hair tied back, Nora presses her fingers on the still-warm printout until her knuckles go white.
general_payoffs: Peg blocks Grant for her in the lobby
The lab proves the half pill holds no medicine, only sugar
Dr. Brandt refused to give Grant her records

title: Signed: Grant Whitlock
youtube_title: Five months of pickups, all signed by the man she trusted.
logline: Nora finally learns what her morning pill was. For five months her husband picked up the real medication. Now she has to decide whether to take it to the police.
hook: Row after row: five months, once a month, the same name in the signature column. Grant Whitlock. Dale pushes up his glasses. "The real pills. Picked up every month."
mid_hook: On the motel bed, Nora lines up three things: the half pill, the lab report, the pickup log. "Every morning, that pill was sugar. That night wasn't bad luck."
extra_hooks: Peg keeps folding laundry. Quietly: "When he heard you were pregnant, his first question was the due date."
conflict: For five months Grant picked up the real pills, and the one on her table every morning was a sugar copy. Now Nora must decide whether to report him, and he is Peg's son.
turn: She always believed that night was her own body, just bad luck. With the three papers side by side, she sees it was arranged, one pill at a time.

cliffhanger.text: Nora slides all three into a manila envelope and presses the flap flat. "I'm going to the police." Peg's hands stop mid-fold. The man Nora means to report is Peg's son.
cliffhanger.question: Will Peg try to stop her?

spectacle: On the white motel sheets, a bitten half pill, a lab report and a pickup log signed with one name, in a row, swept by the red pulse of the neon sign.
glamour_shot: Waist-length hair loose over her shoulders, Nora kneels by the bed squaring each page; red neon catches her eyes from the side, and they are no longer meek.
general_payoffs: The sweet pill is revealed: not Dr. Brandt's prescription but a sugar copy with one stroke of the imprint off; for five months Grant picked up the real pills at the hospital pharmacy
She now holds three exhibits: the half pill, the lab report, the pickup log

title: Evidence, Not a Story
youtube_title: She reported her husband. "Bring me evidence, not a story."
logline: Nora reports Grant to the police with three exhibits. Deputy Prosecutor Marcus Reyes reads the file and declines to file charges. Back at the motel, she can't even pay for the room.
hook: Peg sets down the half-folded shirt. "Then go. I'm coming with you." She picks up her coat and waits at the door first.
mid_hook: Merrow County Prosecutor's Office. Marcus Reyes closes the envelope and pushes it back. "Half a pill and a pickup log don't prove he switched them. Bring me evidence, not a story."
extra_hooks: Nora: "What would be enough?" Reyes stands. "Something that puts his hand on that sugar pill."
conflict: Nora needs the case taken. Reyes needs something that ties Grant directly to the switch: a pickup log proves he collected the real pills, not that he swapped in fake ones.
turn: The audience thinks three exhibits are enough. One line, "Bring me evidence, not a story," sends her back to zero, and at the motel she finds Grant has already cut off every dollar she had.

cliffhanger.text: At the motel desk, Bev slides her cards back one by one. "Declined. This one too." Her new phone buzzes: ACCOUNT FROZEN. Bev holds out a hand. "Tonight's room?" Peg opens her wallet: twenty-five dollars and change.
cliffhanger.question: No money. Where do they sleep?

spectacle: At the end of the prosecutor's long hallway a door shuts; Nora stands in the middle holding the returned envelope as fluorescent tubes run away into the distance.
glamour_shot: On the steps of the county building, wind blowing her long hair across her face, Nora hugs the envelope and looks up at the grey tower, lips pressed tight.
general_payoffs: Peg goes with her to report her own son
She learns what the prosecutor needs: something tying his hand to the pill

title: My Ring
youtube_title: He cut off every dollar. His mother pawned her wedding ring.
logline: Nora has nothing left. Peg pawns her own wedding ring, and at the bank Nora learns Grant moved the money out before that night.
hook: At the pawnshop counter, Peg twists her wedding ring off her finger and sets it down on the glass with a click. "My ring. I'll pawn it if I want."
mid_hook: The bank teller turns the screen. "Mr. Whitlock cancelled your card. The joint account was emptied last week." Nora stares at the date: five days before that night.
extra_hooks: Nora pulls off her own ring to set it beside Peg's. Peg presses her hand flat. "Not yours. Keep it. It'll come in handy."
conflict: First she has to survive: the room, food, tomorrow's bus fare. Her money is frozen, and all they can turn into cash is two wedding rings.
turn: Nora thought the account was frozen after that night. The transfer date says before. He didn't cut her off afterward. He planned it.

cliffhanger.text: Back at the motel, Bev nods at the window. "That black car across the street? Five days now." The door opens. A tall, lean man steps out: dark grey suit, thin-framed glasses, left hand in his coat pocket. He looks up at their window.
cliffhanger.question: Who is the man in the car?

spectacle: Under the pawnshop glass lie old watches and jade bangles; a plain gold band, worn shiny inside from decades on one finger, slides into the light beside them.
glamour_shot: Under the bank's cold white light, Nora leans in to read the transfer date, long hair sliding off her shoulder, her eyes going cold by degrees.
general_payoffs: Peg pawns her own wedding ring, enough to get them through the month
Nora finds the money was moved five days before that night
locations: Across the street from the motel

title: Three Clauses
youtube_title: Day eight: a stranger handed her a contract. Three clauses.
logline: On her eighth day with nowhere to go, a CEO she has never met offers three clauses. The third names the glassworks where she apprenticed at nineteen.
hook: The man stops at the motel door, doesn't lean, holds out a sheet of paper with his right hand. "Ms. Quinn. Elias Ashford." Behind him, a young man in round glasses lifts a tablet: "Ashford Construction. CEO."
mid_hook: Three clauses. "One. This marriage ends on the day Grant Whitlock is sentenced. Two. I open doors. You walk through them. Three. When the Pell case goes to trial, you tell the truth." Her finger stops on "Pell", where she apprenticed at nineteen. "What Pell case?" "You'll find out."
extra_hooks: At the upstairs window, Bev and Peg crowd in to watch, Bev's bowl of peppermints between them. Bev: "Debt collector?" Peg: "Wife collector."
conflict: All she has is the ring money. The prosecutor won't file, and she can't afford a lawyer. A stranger names his terms, spells out that he opens doors but won't walk for her, and won't say why he chose her.
turn: She thinks he wants to buy her evidence. What he wants is someone who will tell the truth in court. And only now does she read the words at the top of the page.

cliffhanger.text: She flips back to the top of the page: MARRIAGE AGREEMENT. She looks up. "Married?" Under the streetlight he looks at her like he's reading the last line of a contract. "Married."
cliffhanger.question: Will she marry a stranger?

spectacle: Under the motel's neon sign, a white sheet snaps in the sea wind, and three lines light up one by one in the red glow.
glamour_shot: Elias under the streetlight: dark grey suit, thin-framed glasses, shoulders straight, the paper in his right hand, his left in his coat pocket, neon red in his lenses.
general_payoffs: The man in the black car steps forward: Elias Ashford, CEO of Ashford Construction

title: He Owes Me
youtube_title: A stranger offered marriage. He wants her ex in prison.
logline: Nora wants to know what this man is after. He wants Grant in prison. His lawyer says clause two is hers. And his reason for choosing Nora is one sentence long.
hook: Nora: "What do you want?" Elias: "Him in prison." A beat. "He owes me."
mid_hook: The black car's rear door opens. A woman with her hair pinned up, black blazer and sneakers, steps out holding three case files. "Two is mine. If he fights for you once, the defense calls you a bought witness."
extra_hooks: Theo, under his breath: "Translation: the boss only opens doors." Dana: "You don't have to translate."
conflict: Nora wants to know what's behind this agreement. Elias will only say Grant owes him, and clause two says he won't fight for her. Every step will be hers.
turn: She took "I open doors" for coldness. One line from Dana changes it: he stays out of it so that when Nora takes the stand, no one can say she was bought.

cliffhanger.text: Her last question: "Why me?" He's already at the car. He looks back once. "Because you'll walk on your own." The door shuts.
cliffhanger.question: Why is he so sure of her?

spectacle: Under the streetlight at the motel door, two figures, one in black and one in white, stand a sheet of paper apart; the black car's windows reflect every light in the harbor.

title: He Didn't Stay
youtube_title: Her ex pulled in. The CEO rolled up his window and left.
logline: Before Nora can decide, Grant's car pulls into the motel lot. Elias, who promised only doors, really does leave her to stand on her own.
hook: Peg charges downstairs in slippers, snatches the agreement, puts on her reading glasses. "Till he's sentenced? And if he isn't?" The car window slides halfway down. Elias: "He will be."
mid_hook: Headlights sweep the lot. Grant's car stops beside the black one. He gets out, buttons his jacket. "Nor. Who's this?" Peg tucks the agreement behind her back. "None of your business."
conflict: Grant has come to take her home and make her sign. Beside her stands a man who says he'll marry her, and whose clause two says he won't fight for her.
turn: The audience expects Elias to step out and back her up. He gives her one look, rolls up the window and drives away. He opened the door. This step is hers.

cliffhanger.text: The black car's taillights turn the corner. Now it's just Nora, Peg and Grant in the lot. He steps closer, voice still warm. "Come home. Sign the papers." She doesn't step back.
cliffhanger.question: Can she stand up to him alone?

general_payoffs: Peg hides the agreement behind her back in front of her son: "None of your business."

title: Shoulder Length
youtube_title: "Tomorrow at ten, I'm filing." That night, she cut her hair.
logline: Nora files for divorce but won't give up the property. That night she cuts her hair to her shoulders and signs the three clauses, and Sienna posts a blank marriage application.
hook: Nora looks at Grant. "Tomorrow, ten a.m. Superior Court. I'm filing for divorce." He smiles, like she's finally given in. "About time."
mid_hook: In the motel bathroom mirror, Peg holds the scissors by Nora's ear. "Cut it and there's no going back." Nora: "I'm not going back." One snip. Long hair falls into the sink.
extra_hooks: Dawn at the motel table, Nora signs the three clauses with Bev's pen, then dials the number on Dana's card. "Signed. I pay my own room and rent." Elias, on the line: "Fine."
conflict: Nora wants the divorce without signing the property away. Grant thinks she'll sign the property agreement too, and she has to let him find out in court that he's wrong.
turn: Grant thinks she's caving. All she files at ten is a divorce petition, the property left for a judge, and the call she made at dawn was to accept a marriage agreement.

cliffhanger.text: Ten a.m., courthouse steps, the stamped petition in her hand: EARLIEST DECREE, 90 DAYS. Her phone lights up with Sienna's new post: a blank marriage application and a pen, captioned "90 days."

title: Two Doors, One Hallway
youtube_title: Divorced in one courtroom, married across the hall.
logline: Ninety days later, the judge enters Nora's divorce, with the property left for trial. She crosses the hall to the County Clerk's office, where Elias is waiting with the marriage licence.
hook: "Ninety days later." The motel room; Peg's ledger, every week paid; Nora taking the seawall stairs without the rail; Nora sketching at the motel table. Washington makes you wait ninety days. Then Superior Court: Leonard Fisk slides the property agreement over with the decree. Nora takes only the decree. "I'll sign the divorce. The house — I'll see you in court."
mid_hook: The judge enters the decree, property reserved for trial. Nora stands and crosses the hall to the County Clerk's office. Elias is already there with the marriage licence, Theo behind him with the files. Peg signs as witness again. "Divorce or wedding, I'm her witness. Both."
extra_hooks: Grant stands in the doorway. "That fast?" Elias takes Nora's arm. "Mr. Whitlock. My wife says she doesn't know you."
Bev signs the second witness line, the second time that morning. "Twice in one day. I want a peppermint." Theo, holding the ring box, hands shaking: "I've never held one of these."
conflict: Grant has brought his lawyer to watch her sign the property away with the divorce. Nora means to end one marriage in a single morning and walk into another that lasts only until he is sentenced.
turn: Grant thinks today she gives up. She takes the divorce, leaves the property for trial, and marries another man in front of him. At the clerk's counter Elias slides over a plain band, today's date engraved inside: "Wear it or don't." She puts it on. And Sienna, whom Grant brought along, won't get the licence she wants.

cliffhanger.text: Outside the courthouse, Sienna waits with a marriage application and a pen. Grant takes the paper, folds it once, twice, and slides it into his breast pocket. "Some other day." Sienna's smile stops.
cliffhanger.question: Will Sienna ever get her day?
